title: QUIC RFC 9000 STREAMS_BLOCKED Frame Focused Proof
purpose: Describe the bounded STREAMS_BLOCKED parser, formatter, and protected receive-advisory proof lane for RFC 9000 Section 19.14.
design_summary: The shared stream-limit frame codec remains the canonical STREAMS_BLOCKED parser and formatter seam. It accepts only one-byte type values 0x16 and 0x17, maps those values to bidirectional and unidirectional stream-limit advisory frames, parses a required Maximum Streams variable-length integer, preserves the advertised stream count through parse and format, and rejects values above the 2^60 stream-count limit. The protected Application Data frame loop now consumes valid incoming STREAMS_BLOCKED frames as ack-eliciting advisory frames without opening a stream and converts malformed STREAMS_BLOCKED encodings into a local FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR close.
data_and_state_considerations: Valid incoming STREAMS_BLOCKED frames are advisory only for this bounded slice: they are parsed, consumed, and acknowledged, but they do not create streams or mutate peer stream limits. Values above the allowed stream-count limit remain invalid at both the parser/formatter seam and the protected receive path.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Type 0x16 maps to bidirectional stream-limit blocking and type 0x17 maps to unidirectional stream-limit blocking.
Non-STREAMS_BLOCKED frame types and non-minimal encodings of 0x16 or 0x17 are rejected by the parser.
Truncated Maximum Streams variable-length integer encodings are rejected.
The parser consumes exactly the STREAMS_BLOCKED frame and leaves trailing frames for the caller.
Maximum Streams values below and equal to 2^60 are accepted; larger values are rejected and close protected packets with FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
alternatives_considered: Broaden ARC-QUIC-RFC9000-0007; rejected because that artifact is scoped to outbound STREAMS_BLOCKED runtime emission, not parser and receiver field-shape proof.
Leave the broad multi-requirement S19P14-0002 tests as the only evidence; rejected because generated triage classified that proof as too broad for requirements 0004 through 0007.
Treat malformed incoming STREAMS_BLOCKED frames as generic parse failure; rejected because RFC 9000 Section 19.14 requires larger encoded values to be connection errors.
risks: This slice does not change outbound stream-open retry or STREAMS_BLOCKED emission scheduling.
This slice does not add public flow-control or stream-limit APIs.
This slice does not claim broader interop readiness beyond the protected Application Data runtime path and frame-codec proof.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers only S19P14 type mapping, frame field shape, stream-count limit handling, and protected receive behavior for malformed STREAMS_BLOCKED frames. Sender-side SHOULD emission and no-open behavior remain owned by the existing runtime-emission lane and follow-up proof.
